facts.quote: X = [LA(αA − αS) + ε(LA + LS)]/(αS − ε − αI) (1.5) where X required thickness of the Invar washer αA temperature expansion coefficient for aluminum αS temperature expansion coefficient for stainless steel ... LA thickness of aluminum flange

facts.claim: Huang et al. compute the net thermal displacement as length times integrated contraction for each component, combined by sum/difference (dL = L x eps; dLtotal = dLSamp + dLSiN - dLSi).
facts.quote: dLSamp = LSamp × εSamp = 80 nm (S1) dLSiN = LSiN × εSiN = 70 nm (S2) dLSi = LSi × εSi = 60 nm (S3) dLtotal = dLSamp + dLSiN −dLSi = 90 nm (S4)

facts.applies_to: Gap/mismatch displacement on cooling 300 K -> 4 K = signed sum of L_i x eps_i along the mechanical path; for two parts of common length L this is Delta L = L (eps_a - eps_b)

notes:
UNITS/SIGN: All si values for contraction are dimensionless (unit '1') integrated contraction eps = (L_ref - L_T)/L_ref; POSITIVE = shrinks on cooling. NIST pages tabulate y = [(L-L293)/L293] x 10^5 (the '105' in quotes is 10^5 with the superscript lost in HTML), so eps = -y x 1e-5. NBS Monograph 29 tabulates 10^5 (L293-LT)/L293 (positive = contraction). Lake Shore Table 4 is 'per 10^4' (printed '104' = 10^4).
REFERENCE TEMPERATURES: NIST, Lake Shore and Monograph 29 use 293 K, EXCEPT Monograph 29 Teflon, which is referenced to 298 K (25 C) because PTFE has a first-order transition near 20 C (footnote h). Van Sciver G-10 values are 300 K -> 4.2 K and approximate ('about'). Weisend's 331e-5 example is 300 -> 4 K.
4 K vs 0 K: Monograph 29 has rows 0, 10, 20 K (no 4 K row). Values at 4 K are taken equal to the 0-20 K plateau; many 0/10 K entries carry footnote a 'Estimated' (Gruneisen correlation). 77 K is not tabulated in Monograph 29; the 80 K row is recorded instead (70 K also quoted for interpolation).
Monograph 29 is a 1961 scanned PDF whose OCR text layer is corrupted, so table-cell quotes were transcribed from rendered page images (300 dpi crops), in table order, with '10^5' for the superscript and 'a' for footnote marker a. Values were checked visually. NIST quotes are the HTML table cell texts in reading order (pipes removed).
COMPUTED values: every 4 K / 77 K value marked COMPUTED was evaluated from the verbatim NIST coefficients with y = a + bT + cT^2 + dT^3 + eT^4 (T > Tlow), y = f (T < Tlow). Results (x1e-5, NIST sign): Al6061 4K -415.45, 77K -388.73; SS304 4K -300.04, 77K -279.89; Ti-6Al-4V 4K -173.61, 77K -162.32; sapphire 4K -78.94 (extrapolated; eq range 15-300 K), 15K -79.14, 77K -77.73; G-10 normal 4K -717.90 (extrapolated; eq range 10-300), 10K -714.60, 77K -642.01; G-10 warp 4K -246.03 (extrapolated; eq range 12-300), 12K -243.99, 77K -214.27; Teflon 4K -2127.31, 77K -1943.55; Invar Fe-36Ni 4K and 77K -40 (constant branch below 80 K; polynomial at 80 K gives -40.21). Fits evaluated at 293 K return small non-zero offsets (Al6061 -0.04, SS304 0.07, Ti64 0.01, sapphire 0.23, G-10 normal -0.79, G-10 warp -3.84, Teflon -3.9, x1e-5).
NOT FOUND on NIST: integrated contraction for OFHC copper and silicon (only dL/dT fits are given; not integrated here), and any expansion data for brass (C26000) and 1100 aluminium. NIST has no fused-silica page.
INVAR CAVEAT: Monograph 29 'Invar' is believed to be 42Ni-0.8Mn-Fe (footnote c), not Fe-36Ni; use the NIST Fe-36Ni value (40e-5) for true Invar 36.
TITANIUM CAVEAT: Monograph 29 and Lake Shore titanium (151e-5) are unalloyed Ti; Ti-6Al-4V comes only from the NIST fit (173.61e-5). Monograph 29 warns its Ti-alloy data (RC-130-B, Ti-150-A) 'may be grossly inaccurate'; not used.
QUARTZ: Lake Shore 'Quartz' is crystalline and anisotropic (a-axis 25e-4, c-axis 10e-4, mean 15e-4). Fused silica is near zero and negative (-8e-5 at 0 K, Monograph 29) and sample-dependent by up to 2e-5 below 180 K.
SILICON: contraction is non-monotonic (negative alpha about 20-120 K): 22e-5 at 0 K (estimated), 23.2e-5 at 80 K, 24.7e-5 at 120 K. Huang et al. quote 0.0208 % (300->4 K), consistent within the 293 vs 300 K reference difference.
CONSISTENCY: Monograph 29 and Lake Shore agree for Cu (326), Al (415 vs 414), brass (384), Ti (151), Si (22), Teflon (2140, though Monograph uses a 298 K reference); Lake Shore 'stainless steel 30' vs Monograph AISI 304 = 296. NIST fits agree with Monograph 29 within about 1-2 % (Al6061 415.45 vs pure Al 415; SS304 300.04 vs 296).
INCONSISTENT SOURCE (not used for values): Weisend Table 1.1 (and the CERN/ESS lecture slides by Weisend) list Cu 326e-5 under 'DeltaL/L (300-100 K)' plus 44e-5 for 100-4 K; 326e-5 is actually the full 293->0 K value in Monograph 29, so that column split appears erroneous. Weisend's 331e-5 stainless example (tc fact) inherits this and is recorded only to evidence the L x (DeltaL/L) usage.
DIFFERENTIAL RELATION: no source found stating literally 'Delta L = L*(eps_a - eps_b)'. Supporting sources: Weisend Eq. 1.5 (term LA(alphaA - alphaS), alpha used as integrated m/m contraction multiplying a length) and Huang et al. arXiv:2201.07780 Supplement Eqs. S1-S4 (dL_i = L_i x eps_i, combined by subtraction). The relation Delta gap = L(eps_a - eps_b) follows directly for a common length L, free contraction and the same reference temperature.
ACCESS NOTES: The Van Sciver and Weisend chapters are Springer book chapters read from copies hosted by JLab and INSPIRE-HEP respectively (DOIs verified via doi.org redirects to link.springer.com). CERN CDS returned a bot-protection page and was not used. An Ekin book copy on a university wiki was not used (not an official open copy).
